summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The four calls stay neutral with low conviction, and the market's own trend has turned down. Nothing here is expected to beat the index or is something to buy; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: The brain looked at its runners again. In old races, picking the strong-looking ones did no better than pulling names from a hat, so it keeps watching with pretend money. The family's real money keeps going into the basket that holds the whole market, a little every week, even when the market has a dull patch.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. The weekly buy of the whole-market fund goes in as usual for money we will leave alone for years, and money we may need soon stays safe. The market's trend has tipped down a little. That is weather, not a reason to stop: steady weekly buying means a dull patch buys a little more for the same amount.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. Last week's bet came out ahead, so the weekly game now stands at one week won and one lost. That is exactly what a coin would do, and it proves nothing yet. This week we place a fresh bet.

Third, a lesson. Two of our names looked better on the chart checklist last week and look worse this week, with nothing new in the businesses. A chart's mood changes faster than a company does.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain

bets.why: A fresh bet for the new week: names above their trend that pass the setup checks without being stretched, against names below their trend whose chart checklist leans down. No rule like this has beaten luck, so it is a learning bet only.

Its report is due in about a day and not confirmed, so the next move rides on one event, and the checklist reward-to-risk is too thin with volume weakening. The Pershing Square fund's disclosed book holds it; that fund's record is too thin to count and this call neither follows nor fights it. Neutral and low, unchanged.
